transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you that brought you here today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I just, well, I came in because... I don't know, it's probably not a huge deal, but I feel like I got this motor running inside me all day. And, um, if I have to sit still—like at church, or out there in the clinic waiting room, or even just sitting at home—I start feeling really trapped. Like I just have to get up or do something. 

I try my best to be respectful and sit quiet, I really do, but it's just hard. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay...
When you feel that restlessness or the need to move, does it come along with feeling anxious, worried, or on edge, or does it feel more like a physical discomfort without the anxiety?

Um, well... I don't really think I feel worried. Like, my mind isn't scared or, you know, on edge about anything bad happening. I hope it's okay to say that, I'm definitely not trying to be difficult or disagree with you. 

It's just... I guess it's more like what you said, a physical thing. My body just wants to go, and if I can't, it just gets real uncomfortable. Like an itch you can't scratch, maybe? I don't want you to think I'm crazy or making things up, it's just this physical pull. I hope I'm answering your question right... is that the kind of thing you were asking?
Can you tell me if this feeling of restlessness or needing to move has been something you’ve experienced most days, and have you noticed it since you were a child or did it start more recently?

Well, um, yes sir... it's been pretty much every day. And, gosh, it's been going on since I was just a little kid. 

I really hope you don't think I was a bad boy or anything, because I always tried my best to be good, but... well, back when I was a boy in school, the teachers were always having to move my seat around. I just couldn't stay put. I'd end up talking out of turn, or I'd get in trouble for jumping up out of my chair before class was even done. 

I feel awful even admitting that to you, because I know it wasn't right and I never wanted to be a bother to my teachers, but my body just wouldn't stay down. Does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm giving you the right information...
As a child, did you have trouble focusing on tasks or often act without thinking, and have these issues continued into your adult life?

Um, well... I don't really think so? I mean, I always tried real hard to pay attention to my teachers and my folks. I never wanted to be disrespectful or ignore anyone, I promise. 

And as for doing things without thinking... gosh, I hope I don't sound like I'm arguing with you, because I know you're the expert here and I don't want to be difficult. I always try my best to think things through and do the right thing. It's just... well, sometimes my body just jumps up or moves before I can catch it, like I was saying before. But my mind is always trying to be good, if that makes sense. 

Even now as a grown man, I feel like I can focus okay on things when I need to... it's just that physical twitchy feeling that gets in the way of me staying put. Is it okay that I don't really have those other problems you mentioned? I really hope I'm still answering your questions right...
Can you tell me if, even now as an adult, you find yourself getting distracted easily, forgetting things often, or having trouble staying organized with tasks or responsibilities?

Oh, um... no sir, I don't believe I have too much trouble with that. I really do try my absolute best to keep track of my things and remember what I'm supposed to be doing. I don't want to sound like I'm bragging or anything, I just... well, I put a lot of effort into staying organized so I don't let anyone down or make a mess of things. 

I hope it's alright that I don't have those particular problems? I know you're asking for a reason, and I'd hate to be giving you the wrong answers or making your job harder. I'm definitely not trying to contradict you. But my memory is usually pretty okay, and I can keep my focus on my responsibilities just fine... it's really just that physical need to move that I can't seem to stop. Is it okay that my answer is no for that one?
Have you ever noticed any shaking or tremors in your hands or other parts of your body, especially when you're at rest?

Oh, um, no sir. I don't think I have any shaking or tremors like that. My hands are pretty steady, I promise. 

I mean, I know I was saying how I have a hard time sitting still and my body always wants to get up and move, but it's not like a... like a sickness kind of shaking, you know? It's just me being a little too energetic, maybe. I really hope I'm not confusing things for you. I definitely don't have any tremors when I'm just sitting or resting... well, when I *can* actually rest, that is. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details so I'm not wasting your time.
Have you ever experienced any sudden, uncontrollable movements or tics, like blinking your eyes over and over, shrugging your shoulders, or making sounds without meaning to?

Oh, um... no sir. I don't believe I do anything like that. I don't make any strange sounds or blink a whole lot, I promise. 

I try really hard to be polite and respectful of the people around me, so I think I'd definitely notice if I was making noises without meaning to. It's really just... well, like I was trying to explain before, it's just my legs and my body needing to get up and walk around or run. But no sudden jerks or sounds like you're talking about. 

I hope it's okay that I keep saying no to these things? I know you're trying to figure me out, and I really appreciate how thorough you are. I just want to be completely honest with you so I don't mess up your evaluation. Am I still doing okay with my answers?
When you're in situations where you really have to stay still, like sitting for a long time or waiting, does that restlessness or physical discomfort get worse?

Oh, um... yes sir. That's actually... well, that's exactly why I came in to see you. 

I just... I feel like I've got this motor running inside me all day long. And if I'm in a situation where I really have to stay put—like sitting at church, or waiting out in the lobby at the clinic, or even just trying to sit quietly at home—I start feeling so... trapped. Like I just absolutely have to get up or do something. 

I try so hard to be good and stay seated, especially at church, because I don't want to be disrespectful or bother anyone. But it just gets so uncomfortable, almost like I'm gonna burst if I don't move. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a nuisance or anything. I really do try my best to hold it in. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope that's helpful for you to know.

When you're at work or trying to complete a task that requires you to sit and focus for a while, do you find it hard to stay on track, or does your mind tend to wander even if your body is able to stay still?

Oh, um... well, I don't really have a job right now, sir. But when it comes to focusing... I try, I really do try to pay attention. 

Like, when the folks at the house are talking through things we need to do—like the ride times for the week, or what we need on the pantry lists, or plans for church—I always start out listening real good. I want to be helpful and do my part, you know? But then... I don't know, my mind just sort of slips off somewhere else. And then I realize I missed pieces of what they said, pieces I really needed to hear to get things right. 

I feel so bad when it happens because I don't want them thinking I don't care about what they're saying. I really do care. I just... my brain just wanders off without my permission, even if I'm sitting there quietly. I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or like I'm not trying hard enough. I really am trying. Does that answer what you were asking, sir?
